source.title: ML-OPF-Bench: Benchmarking Machine Learning for Optimal Power Flow
source.authors: Xin-Yi Liu; Xuan He; Danny H. K. Tsang; Yi-Ze Chen

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It concerns machine learning for optimal power flow, not language-model pretraining.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures data- and compute-scaling behavior in supervised OPF models, a different task from language-model pretraining. Its results bear on the broader beyond-text scaling version, but do not test language-model cross-entropy scaling or parameter-token allocation.
record.gate_note: The study fits power laws to OPF prediction-error and other metric series as training data increases, and reports test error for DNN architectures selected under compute budgets. These are not held-out language-model cross-entropy results. The paper also cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al.; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to held-out prediction error against training-set size for supervised OPF networks. This is a new, non-text setting that bears on whether the power-law form carries over (V5). The Appendix B log-space versus NLS sensitivity fits bear on fit-dependence (V7). There are no language models, so V1–V4 and V6 are untested. The compute-budget sweep reports selected frontier points without a fitted law.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors also note that the 12K-sample selected network beats the 35K-sample DNN in AC but not in DC. They conclude that architecture selection and more data give different gains.
record.recipe_differences: The study fits OPF prediction metrics against training-data size and evaluates selected supervised network architectures under compute budgets; it does not use language-model pretraining loss or the original language-model scaling-law measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Data-fit exponents vary between log-space ordinary least squares and nonlinear least squares. Compute-budget outcomes depend on architecture and can plateau when early stopping prevents using the full budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a fixed 12K-sample training set, the compute frontier of selected DNNs shows diminishing returns. Gain per TFLOP falls from 2.298 to 0.149 pp (AC) and from 2.945 to 0.005 (DC). It plateaus once early stopping caps compute, and wider nets do not consistently help (AC 4×512 0.310% vs 4×128 0.206%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With training data fixed, extra compute and model size yield sharply diminishing and non-monotone gains in small supervised regressors.

fits_no_version.finding: Constraint-violation metrics scale differently from prediction error. DC DNN Pg violation has a positive exponent (0.735, Rlog²=0.461).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Secondary task metrics need not follow the power-law trend of the training-loss-aligned error metric.

record.problems: The scaling experiments are on one 118-bus OPF setting and measure prediction MAE rather than language-model cross-entropy. The compute study reports selected test-error points, not a fitted compute power law; the tested ranges and outcomes do not establish extrapolation to much larger runs.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for constraint-violation scaling or training-time scaling: those measures do not measure the prediction-loss behavior named by V5. Other Appendix B metrics likewise concern feasibility or training cost, not the prediction-error scaling recorded here.

untested.parts: No language models, cross-entropy loss, or parameter/token/compute sweeps over orders of magnitude.
No extrapolation from small to much larger runs; the data range covers only 1K–35K samples.
No compute-optimal parameter/data allocation. Data is fixed in the compute study.
Depth and width vary at fixed data and compute, not at a fixed parameter count.
No parameter or compute power law is fitted. There is no image, video, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regime. Only one 118-bus system is tested, over about 1.5 orders of magnitude of data.
No comparison of parameter counting, schedule, or compute-optimal split. Only the fitting method (log-OLS vs NLS) is varied.

missing.what: AC generator-voltage MAE data-scaling fits are not recorded as rows. DNN α=-0.405 (Rlog² 0.965), KKT -0.265, MU -0.382, LR -0.048. These are prediction-error power laws not declared in rows_left_out.
missing.locator: Appendix B, Data Scaling table (MAE V rows); Figure 7

missing.what: Raw MAE series showing late upticks that bend from a power law: AC DNN 0.173→0.216 at 30K→35K; DC KKT 0.139/0.149→0.253 at 20K/30K→35K.
missing.locator: Appendix D, DC and AC Data Scaling tables

record.verdict_notes: This is an OPF benchmark, not language modelling. Its scaling bearing is limited to a Hestness-style data-scaling fit in one 118-bus setting over about 1.5 decades. The reader's V7 label 'limits_scope' was reversed: fit-method sensitivity is what V7 asserts, so the strong cases support it. LR rows are unlinked from V5 because a linear model is capacity-bottlenecked. The compute rows are frontier selections at fixed data and contain duplicate checkpoints (r12/r13, r16/r17); they are moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No language models, held-out pretraining cross-entropy, or power-law loss sweep over language-model parameters, tokens, and compute.
No tests of predictions from small runs against much larger language-model runs.

The study fixes the OPF training set for its compute study and selects network architectures under budgets; it does not test a language-model parameter/token allocation or a stable compute-optimal split.
It varies depth and width in OPF networks, but does not compare architecture details at a fixed parameter count in language models.
The study tests supervised OPF prediction-error scaling, not language-model pretraining or other modalities of language-model training; it does not test repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream language-model task performance or relationship between language-model pretraining loss and downstream performance.
The study compares log-space and nonlinear least-squares power-law fits for OPF metrics, not language-model cross-entropy exponents or language-model compute-optimal allocations.
